paper_reference.paper_question: 在给定的因果图和一个观测变量集合 Z 下，什么时候可以从观测分布识别干预分布 p(y|do(x))？
paper_reference.target: p(y|do(X=x)) for the declared binary treatment and outcome.
paper_reference.source_location: Pearl (1995), §3.1, Definition 3 and Theorem 1, Eq. (6), pp. 674-675.
paper_reference.formula: If Z satisfies the back-door criterion relative to (X,Y), then p(y|do(x)) = sum_z p(y|x,z) p(z).
conditions: The causal diagram is a DAG with the declared direct edges.
Z contains no descendant of X.
Z blocks every path between X and Y that contains an arrow into X.
The observed joint distribution is available and strictly positive on the declared binary domain.
The intervention sets X=x and leaves the other structural mechanisms unchanged.
what_paper_supports: The graphical back-door criterion is sufficient for identifying the interventional distribution.
The adjustment formula sums over Z and weights by p(z), not by the treatment-group distribution of Z.
A set that includes a descendant of X does not satisfy the criterion.
what_paper_does_not_support: It does not provide a complete general graph-ID algorithm.
It does not identify the target when no back-door set exists.
It does not turn an object collaboration network into a variable causal graph.
It does not make the synthetic business graph a medical fact claim.
